questions.q: The time period $T$ of a simple pendulum of length $l$ is given by $T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}$, where $g$ denotes the acceleration due to gravity. If the length of the pendulum is increased by $1 \%$, then the approximate change in its time period is
questions.solution:
Given, $T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}$ Then, $\frac{d T}{d l}=\frac{2 \pi}{\sqrt{g}} \cdot \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{l}}=\frac{T}{\sqrt{l}} \cdot \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{l}} \quad\left[\because T=\frac{2 \pi}{\sqrt{g}} \cdot \sqrt{l}\right]$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d T}{d l}=\frac{T}{2 l} & \Rightarrow \frac{d T}{T}=\frac{1}{2} \frac{d l}{l} \\
\text { Given, } \frac{d l}{l} \times 100 & =1 \Rightarrow \frac{d l}{l}=\frac{1}{100} \\
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d T}{T} & =\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{100} \\
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d T}{T} \times 100 & =\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{100} \times 100=\frac{1}{2}=0.5 \%
\end{aligned}

$\therefore$ Change in its time period $T$ is $0.5 \%$.

questions.solution:

Differentiating w.r.t. \(x\), we get
\(\frac{d y}{d x}=\cos x\)
If tangent to \(y=\sin x\) meet at \((h, k)\)
\(\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)_{(h, k)}=\cos h\)
\(\therefore\) Equation of tangent is \(\cos h(x-h)=y-k\) Since, tangent is passing through (origin).
\(\therefore \quad h \cos h=k\)
But given curve is passing through \((h, k)\)
\(\begin{aligned}
k=\sin h \Rightarrow & \cos h=\sqrt{1-k^2} \\

\Rightarrow & h^2-k^2=h^2 k^2
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, locus of point of contact is \(x^2-y^2=x^2 y^2\)

questions.solution:
The shortest distance between the line and curve occurs when the tangent to the curve is parallel to the given line.

Rewriting the line $y-x=1$ in standard form gives $x-y+1=0$, which has slope $m_L = 1$.

For the curve $x=y^2$, differentiating yields $\frac{dx}{dy} = 2y$, so the tangent slope is $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{2y}$. Setting this equal to the line's slope gives $\frac{1}{2y} = 1$, so $y = \frac{1}{2}$. The corresponding x-coordinate is $x = y^2 = \frac{1}{4}$.

The distance from point $\left(\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{2}\right)$ to the line $x-y+1=0$ is:

$D = \frac{\left|1\cdot\frac{1}{4} -1\cdot\frac{1}{2} +1\right|}{\sqrt{1^2 + (-1)^2}} = \frac{\frac{3}{4}}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{8}$

The shortest distance is $\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{8}$.
